I’m reading the fixed LAYOUT-002 inputs and applying the repository’s design-evidence and review-validation skills. I’ll quantify the forward gap and distinguish published ALLEGRO design values from the pinned code.

For the earlier barrel follow-up, the independent finite-box check intersected the ray with each silicon box in sector-local coordinates:

```python
theta = (phi + math.pi/16) % (math.pi/8) - math.pi/16
u_slope = math.tan(theta)
z_slope = math.sinh(eta) / math.cos(theta)
radius = 1700 + 10.9*layer_index + 2.5
lo, hi = radius - 0.25, radius + 0.25
for slope, center in ((u_slope, module_u), (z_slope, module_z)):
    if slope == 0:
        if abs(center) > 44:
            lo, hi = 1, 0
            break
    else:
        a, b = sorted(((center-44)/slope, (center+44)/slope))
        lo, hi = max(lo, a), min(hi, b)
hit = hi > lo + 1e-9
```

This matched all 60 saved native rays. The prism mock exposed `GetScale(i)=2`, `GetXOffset(i)=100`, `GetYOffset(i)=0`, `GetZ(i)=[-5,5]`, and the four vertices of a 2×2 square. The existing capacity helper called only `GetNvert`, `GetX`, `GetY` and `GetZ`; it returned 40 instead of the scaled volume 160.

The translated ALLEGRO endcap has no active wheel coverage at η4. Its first built blade starts at 410 mm; at the moved sampling front, η4 reaches only 146.94 mm. The wheel envelopes permit some sampling up to η≈3.082, with rapidly decreasing depth beyond η≈2.976. A smaller aperture alone would also violate blade-angle and gap constraints.

I verified the service slides. Their ASIC power figures, 14 W CFEB example and 120 kW cooling study describe different scopes and cannot be combined into one established operating budget.

Keeping the source barrel radii and 1536 planes avoids changing the established gap geometry. There is still a material-version choice to make: the pinned XML specifies 0.1 mm total steel cladding, or 50 µm per face, while the published cold-test baseline prefers 100 µm per face. Increasing the cladding changes the plate-spacing closure and must be reflected in the gaps or plane count.

The axial extension also needs a readout change. Keeping the source theta origin `0.5902785 rad` while extending the active half-length to about 3.87–3.90 m gives front-end directions near `0.512–0.508 rad`, which map to negative theta bins in the current unsigned field. The candidate must update the theta origin, recount channels and test cell-ID round trips at both axial ends.

**LAYOUT002-PhysVal-input reviewed `e33ae62ce16592c26c581c5311c4dc493d9714b1`, read-only.** I also read the prior assessment at `a3dffd327e47cc65dfacb33cf6b7219923683166` and independently inspected official k4geo `e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb`. No edits, native jobs, installations or software adoption.

**Retaining ALLEGRO’s sampling radii and 1536 barrel planes is a coherent prototype starting point. Extending its length and translating its endcaps still require new readout, service and forward-coverage definitions.**

- **FACT — barrel sampling and readout.** Pinned sampling radii are **2172.8–2578.3 mm**, radial depth **405.5 mm**; inclined electrode length is **573.94 mm**, angle **50.18°**. The inner **2.492 mm sensitive thickness represents both gaps**, approximately **1.246 mm per side**. There are eleven longitudinal compartments; the default readout merges two adjacent electrode modules and uses approximately **9.817 mrad theta bins**, with **2.454 mrad strips in compartment 1**. Preserve the first compartment’s replacement of Pb by LAr. These are not forty-eight SiW layers. [Pinned barrel XML, lines 18–145](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/FCCee/ALLEGRO/compact/ALLEGRO_o1_v03/ECalBarrel_thetamodulemerged.xml#L18)

- **P1 — axial extension needs a new theta origin.** The existing readout uses `offset_theta=0.5902785 rad` and unsigned `theta:10`. Extending the active half-length from **3066.2** to **3866.2–3900 mm** gives front-end polar angles **0.5120–0.5083 rad**, requesting approximately **−32/−33 raw theta bins**. Update the origin, merging alignment and channel inventory; check both axial ends. Simply increasing `BarECal_dz` is insufficient. [Segmentation, lines 166–195](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/detectorSegmentations/src/FCCSWGridModuleThetaMerged_k4geo.cpp#L166)

- **P1 — distinguish simulated cladding from the cold-test baseline.** Pinned XML has **0.1 mm total steel**, divided into **50 µm per face**, plus 0.1 mm total glue. The published cold-test baseline prefers **100 µm steel per face**. Changing this requires a new spacing/material closure. The driver enforces  
  `N = round(π / asin((t_abs + t_PCB + g_total)/(2 Rin cos α)))`.  
  At unchanged radii, increasing total steel by 0.1 mm while retaining 1536 planes reduces each inner gap by approximately **0.05 mm** unless another parameter changes. [Driver, lines 289–319 and 471–472](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/detector/calorimeter/ECalBarrel_NobleLiquid_InclinedTrapezoids_o1_v03_geo.cpp#L289), [published mechanics, PDF5]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

- **FACT — turbine bounds and identities.** The **650 mm package**, translated to front **3950 mm**, contains sampling at **4010–4460 mm**. Built blade intervals are:

  | Wheel | Blade radii | Unit cells |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 410–764.260 mm | 384 |
  | 2 | 774.260–1460.235 mm | 720 |
  | 3 | 1470.235–2790 mm | 1360 |

  Nominal XML `400–2750 mm` does not describe these actual blade bounds. Readout has **10 axial bins** and **10/14/34 radial bins**, whereas calibration geometry uses **5/1/1 axial subdivisions**. The default combinatorial readout grid has **601,600 addresses per endcap**, not an established installed-channel bill. Its `layer` field identifies calibration subdivisions and is recalculated from `wheel/rho/z`; it is not eleven universal shower-depth layers. [Endcap XML](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/FCCee/ALLEGRO/compact/ALLEGRO_o1_v03/ECalEndcaps_Turbine_o1_v03.xml), [wheel construction](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/detector/calorimeter/ECalEndcap_Turbine_o1_v03_geo.cpp#L784)

- **INFERENCE — forward reach after translation.** For straight IP rays, `r=z/sinh|η|`. Wheel envelopes permit any sampling over approximately **1.159<|η|<3.082**. Full axial depth lies within inner/outer bounds only for approximately **1.248≤|η|≤2.976**, with additional losses where rays cross wheel-support strips.

  | \|η\| | Axial sampling-window fraction* | Approximate absorber-midplane crossings** |
  |---:|---:|---:|
  | 1.20 | 44.75% | 14.36 |
  | 1.75 | 93.80% | 48.21 |
  | 2.40 | 87.85% | 40.59 |
  | 2.75 | 100% | 45.12 |
  | 3.00 | 78.37% | 44.55 |
  | 3.05 | 31.35% | 18.41 |
  | 3.08 | 1.99% | 1.25 |
  | 4.00 | 0% | 0 |

  *Bounds-only calculation, excluding supports between wheels; not efficiency.  
  **Zero-thickness plane model averaged over continuous azimuthal phase; not native transport or X₀.

  I used clipped wheel intervals in z and the source turbine relation  
  `ψ(z)=asin((z−4235)sinhη/(z tan49°))`, giving `N Δψ/(2π)` crossings per traversed wheel. [Source phi relation, lines 259–285](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/detectorSegmentations/src/FCCSWEndcapTurbine_k4geo.cpp#L259)

  At η4, front/rear radii are **146.94/163.43 mm**. A marked later FCal therefore remains necessary. Merely shrinking the aperture is insufficient: **450 mm depth at 49° requires blade inner radius ≥195.59 mm**, and retained first-wheel counts/thicknesses additionally require approximately **210.55 mm for positive gaps**. The source driver can return without building an invalid wheel, so construction success alone cannot certify complete wheels. [Driver guard and gap calculation, lines 102–152](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/e1ba7bc3e0d7291ebe3f6a02abfa784f879e36cb/detector/calorimeter/ECalEndcap_Turbine_o1_v03_geo.cpp#L102)

- **FACT — service evidence exists, but describes developing scenarios.** January 2026 PDF11 gives CHARMS250 **<10 mW/channel**, including approximately **5.5 mW simulated analog power**, and contrasts approximately **2 million warm cables** with cold digitization. September PDF11–13 gives **6–11 mW/channel**, a **14 W CFEB example**, and CALOROC1C **36 channels/~10 mW per channel**. PDF38 describes **20,000-wire feedthrough R&D**, including small-sample thermal-cycle/leak tests. These do not establish a complete flange schedule or installed power budget. [January overview]([external URL redacted; see source journal]), [September summary]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

  July PDF20/44 studies **120 kW**, **1.07 kg/s two-phase nitrogen**, **48×6 m runs with 18 mm ID**, and pressure drop **<0.03 bar**. It explicitly excludes global cooling design. Later pages discuss **96 half-length segments**, thermal-contact assumptions and unresolved reinforcement. Preserve these scenario distinctions; do not combine ASIC-only power, CFEB examples and complete cooling-study loads into one “measured” budget. [Thermal study]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

Minimum validation before stronger claims: verify actual wheel/plate counts and positive gap thickness everywhere; test all readout address limits and cell-position round trips; compare finite-volume rays against analytic bounds at both ends, wheel edges, barrel/endcap transitions and η≈3–4; resolve azimuthal cell phases sufficiently to avoid coarse-grid aliasing; retain constituent mass and directional X₀/λ maps; and distinguish sparse positive-energy readout tests from shower/noise/calibration performance. An inner 3 T coil requires its own upstream-material and field treatment—the source ECAL’s 2 T field must not be copied as nODD’s installed field.

The assigned manifest contains **no ALLEGRO entries**; the coordinator must catalogue these sources. The tracked checkout was clean; only the coordinator’s two untracked journal files were present.

```python
for slope, center in ((math.tan(theta), module_u),
                      (math.sinh(eta)/math.cos(theta), module_z)):
    if slope == 0:
        if abs(center) > 44:
            lo, hi = 1, 0
            break
    else:
        a, b = sorted(((center-44)/slope, (center+44)/slope))
        lo, hi = max(lo, a), min(hi, b)
hit = hi > lo + 1e-9
```

It matched all sixty saved barrel rays. The prism mock’s omitted accessors were `GetScale(i)=2`, `GetXOffset(i)=100`, `GetYOffset(i)=0`; actual validation should require two centred, zero-offset, unit-scale sections.
